hooks.text: One battered spacecraft has been mapping Mars for twenty-three years.
How has one NASA robot survived Mars for twenty-three years?
Most people think robots die quickly in the Martian desert.

title: The Survivor of the Red Planet
description: NASA's 2001 Mars Odyssey has outlasted nearly every mission at Mars, serving as a critical lifeline for over two decades.

beats.text: One battered spacecraft has been mapping Mars for twenty-three years.
beats.visual: NASA artist's concept of the 2001 Mars Odyssey spacecraft in orbit, 2001

beats.text: Most people think robots die quickly in that harsh desert.
beats.visual: Mars global view, NASA Viking mosaic, 1980

beats.text: But Arthur C. Clarke personally blessed this mission’s name.
beats.visual: Portrait photograph of author Arthur C. Clarke, 1984

beats.text: To reach orbit, it surfed the thin Martian atmosphere to slow down.
beats.visual: Diagram of spacecraft aerobraking at Mars, NASA illustration

beats.text: A solar storm fried its radiation sensor in 2003.
beats.visual: NASA diagram of solar particle event hitting spacecraft

beats.text: This legend even guided Curiosity safely through the seven minutes of terror.
beats.visual: Illustration of Curiosity rover landing during the sky crane phase, 2012

beats.text: It serves as an interplanetary internet, relaying rover data.
beats.visual: Graphic showing Mars Odyssey relaying signals from the surface to Earth, NASA

beats.text: That is why one battered spacecraft has been mapping Mars for twenty-three years.
beats.visual: Global thermal map of Mars created by the THEMIS instrument

better_than_last: This episode uses the myth_vs_fact structure to contrast perceived fragility with the probe's 23-year lifespan while incorporating the reviewer-requested internet relay line in beat 7.
